# Internal delegation briefs and handbacks

Date: 2026-10-13. This records-only prerequisite supports the queued W4/D86
delegation work and confirmed [D81](DECISIONS.md). It installs no launcher,
model tool, prompt, route, worker action, approval or grant. A prepared record
does not prove dispatch or a running child. An unfinished intent retains an
unknown terminal outcome; replay does not authorize repeating possible effects.

The [plans/delegation specification](specs/plans-and-delegation.md) remains a
draft beyond its confirmed requirements. The record vocabulary below is an
explicit engineering increment, not adoption of all PD-11–22 defaults. No
concurrency/depth, one-correction-call, model fallback, cost, approval, question
or resume policy is enabled.

## Identity and authority

[`DelegationRecords`](../packages/orchestrator/src/sandbox_science/orchestrator/delegation_records.py)
borrows an existing canonical `DocumentStore`. Every operation has separate
trusted attribution. `ParentAuthority` binds project, session, environment and
original parent run. `HandbackAuthority` additionally binds the original
delegation and generated child-run IDs. Construction is not authentication;
model JSON, a stored record or a reference claim cannot manufacture authority.
A future caller must derive it from its actual authenticated control context.

The parent binding cannot silently change environments. IDs are bounded ASCII;
the parent and child cannot impersonate USER or be the same run. Preparation
atomically allocates one delegation ID and child-run ID after checking replay.
No session record, workspace directory, environment or kernel is created. This
store is scoped to a logical session, not an opaque cross-request open lifetime.
Historical reads/replays confer no current open-session or execution eligibility.

Briefs retain task/context-summary text, bounded same-project reference claims,
an optional historical plan/track/step-fingerprint pin, requested profile/model
alias pins and explicit finite requested limits. These are intentions and data,
not applied settings, a skill loader, tool selection, current delegated-progress
grant, verified evidence or resource access. No parent transcript, private
endpoint/configuration or credential field is accepted. An unknown resolved
model stays null in the trusted host observation.

## Operations, raw data and immutable receipts

`prepare(authority, operation_id, brief)` records intent only.
`finish(authority, operation_id, expected_revision=1, observation, raw_payload)`
records one terminal host observation and the child's optional structured data.
`get(parent_authority, delegation_id)` returns the exact historical prepared
mutation, optional outcome and separate original raw bytes.
`list(parent_authority, after=0, target=None, limit=8)` pages a pinned parent-local
event prefix with actual continuation; another parent's activity creates no gaps.

Each immutable stored mutation is also its event and historical receipt. Its
action, operation ID, canonical request hash, original identity and scoped
sequence commit in one row. Exact replay returns that original receipt unchanged;
the same operation with different content conflicts. A terminal outcome cannot
be overwritten, and a finish operation cannot name another child. There is no
mutable current projection, ACK queue, dispatch state or automatic reconciliation.

Host `ended` is one of `returned`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `limit_reached` or
`interrupted`, supplied only through the separate trusted controller input.
Child `status` is `complete`, `partial` or `blocked`; summary, result pins,
deviations and open questions are all explicit required fields in
`sandbox-delegation-result-1`. They remain assertions. A child `complete` cannot
change a host failure, and a child `blocked` is not inferred to be a host failure.
Neither changes plan status, scientific findings, publications or permissions.

Original raw `None`, `b''`, invalid UTF-8 and malformed/duplicate JSON remain
distinct. The raw bytes are immutable; their exact length/hash enter the request
identity. The derived result is strictly validated from those bytes. Missing,
invalid or over-budget derived data stays null with a fixed validation code;
fields are never filled in and the host ending remains unchanged. No correction
model call is made. Reads rederive the result and bind every stored mutation's
operation/hash to its own authoritative fields. These are coherence checks, not
cryptographic authenticity against an administrator rewriting all database state.

`get` returns Python bytes, including arbitrary non-UTF-8 values. It defines no
HTTP/JSON transport for them. A later consumer must choose and bound a binary
representation explicitly; these bytes must not be implicitly decoded, executed
or rendered as trusted markup. Stored Markdown/LaTeX/source text is inert data.

## Storage, initialization and ownership

The constructor defaults to `initialize=False`: a wholly absent namespace is
reported not found. Explicit trusted first setup may use `initialize=True`.
Creation is transactional; concurrent initializers observe the same completed
schema. Partial schemas or unsupported versions refuse, including during explicit
initialization. Readonly callers never add this namespace or its schema. An
absent legacy namespace has no invented history. Complete removal of every
namespace table is not distinguishable from prior absence without an external
retained initialization proof; explicit initialization is not such a proof and
must not be used as automatic lost-history recovery.

| Bound | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical brief | 64 KiB |
| Original raw handback | 64 KiB |
| Canonical validated result | 8 KiB |
| Metadata per immutable mutation | 96 KiB |
| Reference claims per brief/result | 32 |
| Event page | At most eight items and 128 KiB complete canonical metadata |
| Default retained delegations | 256/project; 1,024/global |
| Default logical retained bytes | 64 MiB/project; 256 MiB/global |

These are storage safety bounds, not concurrent-agent defaults. Requested turns,
wall time and output-token bounds must be explicit and are not enforced runtime
budgets. Typed host copies are checked before overridable methods or aggregate
JSON encoding, with an exact UTF-8/escaping budget and finite depth/node counts.
Raw payloads refuse their type/size before write admission. SQL projects bounded
types and byte prefixes before Python parsing, preserving empty BLOBs explicitly.
Every read checks its row's recorded byte charge and raw/derived/request identity.

There is no unresolved eviction or compaction. One write transaction checks
retained counts and bytes before and after append. Every mutation/event/receipt
row, raw byte, stored variable column and fixed row reservation counts; the
namespace metadata has a fixed global reservation. Orphans and invalid retained
accounting refuse rather than creating capacity. These are logical accounting
bounds, not a claim about SQLite page/index allocation, RSS or arbitrary external
database growth. A full quota can refuse a terminal append while keeping its
original intent unresolved; callers must not invent a terminal result.

The store owns no connection, executor, thread, asynchronous task or close method.
All work is synchronous under the borrowed store's read/write transactions.
Cancelling a future does not prove admitted SQL stopped. A future async adapter
must retain actual queue/task/file/connection ownership and drain through timeout,
repeated cancellation and shutdown before closing its owner. No generic lifetime
or cancellation change is made here. The owner's existing lock serializes close
with a write already admitted under that lock; this is not a queue-drain guarantee
for future adapters or a terminal-close API.

## Required later integration and local proof

D81 requires each child to use its session's environment with its own kernels.
Today's `ExecutionContext` has no run-to-kernel identity, and the worker keys
kernels by `(session, language)`. A later explicit run/kernel protocol, lineage and
cancellation-scope increment is required before delegated Python/Sage calls.
Creating fake sessions to get separate kernels would violate D81. Later launcher,
role/tool restrictions, fresh plan/session checks, original handback prompts,
successful-model delivery, save/ACK, cancellation/restart reconciliation, GUI and
real worker acceptance remain separate.

Focused isolated control-store tests exercise exact identity and raw retention,
host/result separation, missing fields, replay/substitution, two-connection
concurrency, quota/rollback, corrupt-row prefetch, scoped paging, historical pins,
strict copied/subtyped inputs and actual admitted-write/owner-close ordering.
They start no model, provider, service, browser or VM and establish no live
delegated-run behavior. Combined gates, independent review and delivery belong
to root integration.

Local author validation: 56 new focused cases and 233 affected record/plan/document/
project/tool cases pass on Python 3.13. Whole-orchestrator typing, scoped Ruff and
format, locked dependency sync and the 75-distribution license check pass. The
first focused run retained 51 passes and one empty-BLOB projection failure;
the corrected bounded SQL explicitly preserves `b''`. Original unsuccessful
style/type logs and that source snapshot remain separate from final evidence.

# Next bounded slice: internal delegation briefs and structured handbacks

Read-only assessment, 2026-10-13, at signed clean planning-delivery head `a3b236e30b0d589bb2bdc18363bcb2a745d5028b`, integrating delivered actual main `65989b57f3ed0d258e3b71f1efee3ba1836787d2`. This is a recommendation for root's next assignment, not implementation or a completion claim. Existing planning and inventory source/report freezes remain untouched.

## Recommendation and authority

Implement an **internal immutable delegation brief/handback record store**, with no launcher, worker call, new tool, route or grant. It is the smallest useful prerequisite for the explicitly queued W4/D86 delegated tracks/outcomes item (`.agents/BACKLOG.md:160`). It establishes durable parent/child identity and exact returned-data handling before any child can execute. Root can authorize the small record contract as an engineering increment; it does not require inventing an end-user approval gate.

D81 is confirmed (`docs/DECISIONS.md:87`): a child is a run in its existing session, with that session's workspace/environment/grants and its own kernels; a new environment is a later opt-in. D86 confirms planning/live progress and original role/lifecycle prompts (`docs/DECISIONS.md:93`). The detailed plans/delegation spec is still a draft (`docs/specs/plans-and-delegation.md:3–5`). Its PD-11–22 brief/outcome language is design guidance for this proposed contract, **not a claim that its defaults or all policies were approved**. In particular this slice implements no depth-one/four-concurrent default, automatic one-repair-call rule, role-model fallback, cost policy, approval decision, question routing or resume policy.

## Current implementation supports the prerequisite, not live delegation

- `session_plans.py:81–118,1020–1091` already distinguishes trusted MAIN/USER/delegated attribution and limits delegated progress to an exact current `PlanRef` and track. The core deliberately says construction is not authentication. Revisions/moves invalidate the old progress grant. `PlanTools` constructs MAIN-only authority (`plan_tools.py:225–227`); no delegated adapter/launcher is installed.
- `SessionPlans` borrows canonical `DocumentStore` transactions and supports bounded readonly history without DDL (`session_plans.py:449–497`). This is a suitable local-store pattern. A new synchronous store must borrow the owner's lifetime; any future async adapter must own and drain admitted SQL before close.
- `RunRecord` is the existing saved conversation (`projects.py:169`), with strict MAIN input and kernel notice coherence. Do not reinterpret or migrate its old records as delegated executions. `ExecutionContext` has project/session/environment/actor, **no distinct run/kernel identity** (`packages/contracts/src/sandbox_science/contracts/context.py:9–23`).
- Worker kernels remain keyed by `(session, language)` (`packages/worker/src/sandbox_science/worker/executor.py:2465–2472`). Starting a child with today's context would share the parent's kernel, violating D81. A later explicit run-to-kernel protocol/lineage/cancel scope increment is mandatory before real delegated Python/Sage execution. Do not create a fake session ID to evade it.

## Three owned paths and proposed contract

Own only new `packages/orchestrator/src/sandbox_science/orchestrator/delegation_records.py`, its `tests/test_delegation_records.py`, and `docs/DELEGATION-RECORDS.md`. Internal strict DTOs can live with the store, as they do in `SessionPlans`; no public contracts/ProjectStore/loop/CLI/worker/frontend edits are needed.

Proposed internal operations are `prepare(trusted_parent, operation_id, brief)`, `finish(trusted_controller, delegation_id, expected_revision, observation, raw_payload)` and scoped `get/list`. A receipt identifies the exact immutable historical record; replay is not proof the current plan/session is still eligible to run. Preparation records intent only, never `running` or actual dispatch. It allocates one delegation ID and child-run ID inside the atomic replay/write boundary.

The separate trusted attribution supplies project/session/environment/parent run and role. Request JSON cannot select an actor or another session/environment. Record an optional exact plan/track reference and step fingerprints as **historical brief pins**, not a new live progress grant; a later launcher must recheck the current plan and scope. Both parent and child remain in the same session; no SessionRecord, directory, environment or kernel is created.

An immutable brief contains task/context-summary text, bounded same-project typed input references, fixed output-schema version, and explicitly supplied finite requested limits/profile metadata. Those are recorded intentions, not effective grants or applied settings. Unknown resolved model remains null. No private endpoint, key, token, credential digest or parent transcript is stored.

An outcome separates trusted host observation (`returned|failed|cancelled|limit_reached|interrupted`) from the child's optional validated assertion (`complete|partial|blocked`, summary, typed result references, deviations, open questions). Retain the bounded original returned bytes unchanged, including invalid UTF-8/JSON if supplied; parse only a bounded copy for the fixed versioned result schema. Retain fixed validation error codes, not arbitrary exception text. Never manufacture omitted fields, interpret child `blocked` as a host failure, overwrite the first terminal record, or automatically update plan completion/findings/publications. Parent interpretation is separate data. No correction model call or outcome transport is wired.

Suggested engineering bounds: brief64KiB, raw handback64KiB, derived/result metadata8KiB, references32, list pages8/complete response128KiB; explicit configurable finite retained counts and actual aggregate-byte quotas, e.g. project256/64MiB and global1024/256MiB. These are storage safety limits, not the draft concurrent-agent policy. All rows/receipts/projections/events count; no unresolved eviction. Reject before allocation/encoding where possible. Use exact builtin/model validation, SQL type/length prefetch guards, duplicate-key refusal for structured JSON, bounded corrupt reads, canonical scope-local replay digests and atomic receipt/event/projection/quota updates. An absent readonly namespace stays absent; partial schema/corruption refuses rather than silently initializing history.

## Meaningful proof and independent review

Use isolated real `DocumentStore` fixtures, not services/models: atomic prepare/reopen replay without allocating a second child; same-op changed payload conflict; foreign project/session/parent/child impersonation and copied/subtyped DTOs; exact raw malformed/duplicate JSON retention with no invented result; host-ending versus child-result distinction; terminal overwrite/CAS race; historical track pin after USER revision without obtaining current grant; NULL unknown model; reader absent/legacy/partial schema and20MiB corrupt-row prefetch; quotas including receipts and concurrent two-connection reservation; rollback/commit-fault and reopening exact immutable receipts; list scope/order/actual continuation. Assert no ProjectStore session/environment creation and no changes to existing prompts, tool lists, RunRecord parsing or plan behavior.

A different agent should review raw-versus-derived coherence, operation/actor substitution, quota accounting and replay from an independently opened database, then root can run the combined gates. This prerequisite needs **no external model configuration, protected-filesystem assumption, VM, browser or live worker acceptance**. A tiny local scripted store composition is sufficient and must be labeled accordingly. Live child calls/handback injection/save-ACK, cancellation/restart reconciliation, own-kernel separation and original handback prompts belong to later independently reviewed integration, with actual worker acceptance before execution is enabled.

This advances the existing D86 queue without depending on the blocked real-model evaluation configuration or the trusted protected staging/filesystem proof still required for export replacement. No further user decision is needed for this records-only proposal once root selects its explicit scope; unresolved draft choices remain deferred, not silently converted into product policy.

def brief(**changes: object) -> DelegationBrief:
    return DelegationBrief(

            "inputs": (),

def controller(prepared: DelegationMutation) -> HandbackAuthority:

        parent_run_id=prepared.parent_run_id,
        delegation_id=prepared.delegation_id,
        child_run_id=prepared.child_run_id,

def returned(**changes: object) -> bytes:

            "summary": "One check remains",
            "results": [],
            "deviations": [],

def test_actual_admitted_write_holds_borrowed_owner_until_commit(records, documents, monkeypatch):

        threading.Event(),

        threading.Event(),
    )

    def close():

        closed.set()

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
        write = pool.submit(prepared, records)
        assert entered.wait(5)
        assert write.cancel() is False  # Actual admitted Python/SQL work is still running.
        closing = pool.submit(close)
        assert close_started.wait(5)
        assert closed.wait(0.03) is False
        release.set()
        value = write.result(timeout=5)
        closing.result(timeout=5)
    assert closed.is_set()
    # The owner permits an intentional reopen; the module did not close it itself.
    assert records.get(parent(), value.delegation_id).prepared == value
